entries.template: A committee of {selectedWomen} women and {selectedMen} men is chosen from {womenCount} women and {menCount} men. In how many ways can the committee be formed and then assigned a chairperson and a secretary?

A committee of {selectedWomen} women and {selectedMen} men is selected from {womenCount} women and {menCount} men. If the chairperson must be a woman, in how many ways can the committee, chairperson and secretary be chosen?

A committee containing {selectedWomen} women and {selectedMen} men is selected from {womenCount} women and {menCount} men. In how many ways can a woman be appointed chairperson and a man be appointed secretary?
A committee of {committeeSize} is chosen from {totalCount} people, with one specified person compulsory. In how many ways can the committee then be assigned a chairperson and a secretary?

A committee of {selectedWomen} women and {selectedMen} men is selected from {womenCount} women and {menCount} men. The chairperson and treasurer must be women, while the secretary must be a man. How many complete selections and appointments are possible?
From {totalCount} distinct people, {arrangementCount} are selected and arranged in a row. If two specified people must both be selected, how many arrangements are possible?
From {totalCount} distinct people, {arrangementCount} are selected and arranged in a row. If two specified people must both be excluded, how many arrangements are possible?
From {womenCount} women and {menCount} men, exactly {selectedWomen} women and {selectedMen} men are selected and arranged in a row. How many arrangements are possible?

From {womenCount} women and {menCount} men, exactly {selectedWomen} women and {selectedMen} men are selected and seated around a round table. How many seatings are possible when rotations are identical?

From {womenCount} women and {menCount} men, exactly {selectedWomen} women and {selectedMen} men are selected for a round table. One specified woman and one specified man must be selected and must sit together. How many seatings are possible when rotations are identical?

From {totalCount} distinct ornaments, {arrangementCount} are selected for a reversible ring, and one specified ornament must be selected. How many rings are possible when rotations and reflections are identical?
In how many permutations of {objectCount} distinct objects is no object left in its original position?
In how many permutations of {objectCount} distinct objects are exactly {fixedCount} objects left in their original positions?
In how many permutations of {objectCount} distinct objects is at least one object left in its original position?
For two specified objects among {objectCount} distinct objects, in how many permutations is exactly one of the two left in its original position?
For two specified objects among {objectCount} distinct objects, in how many permutations is neither of the two left in its original position?
A shortest grid path requires {rightSteps} moves to the right and {upSteps} moves upward. How many shortest paths are possible?
A shortest path from \((0,0)\) to \(({rightSteps},{upSteps})\) must pass through \(({pointX},{pointY})\). How many such paths are possible?
A shortest path from \((0,0)\) to \(({rightSteps},{upSteps})\) must avoid \(({pointX},{pointY})\). How many such paths are possible?
A shortest path from \((0,0)\) to \(({rightSteps},{upSteps})\) must pass through at least one of \(({firstX},{firstY})\) and \(({secondX},{secondY})\). How many such paths are possible?
In how many ways can {objectCount} identical objects be placed in three labelled boxes whose maximum capacities are {firstCapacity}, {secondCapacity} and {thirdCapacity}?

In how many ways can {objectCount} identical objects be placed in three labelled boxes if their respective minimums are {firstMinimum}, {secondMinimum}, {thirdMinimum} and their maximums are {firstCapacity}, {secondCapacity}, {thirdCapacity}?
In how many ways can {objectCount} distinct objects be assigned to three labelled boxes whose maximum capacities are {firstCapacity}, {secondCapacity} and {thirdCapacity}?
In how many ways can {redCount} identical red balls and {blueCount} identical blue balls be distributed among {boxCount} labelled boxes when boxes may be empty?
In how many ways can {redCount} identical red balls and {blueCount} identical blue balls be distributed among {boxCount} labelled boxes if every box must receive at least one ball in total?
In how many ways can {totalCount} distinct people be divided into {teamCount} named teams of {teamSize} each and then one captain be chosen for every team?
In how many ways can {totalCount} distinct people be divided into {teamCount} unnamed teams of {teamSize} each and then one captain be chosen for every team?

There are {womenCount} women and {menCount} men. They are divided into two named teams of {teamSize} each, with Team A containing exactly {teamAWomen} women. Afterward, a captain is chosen for each team. How many outcomes are possible?
